parts.text:
A nucleus $Z$ undergoes nuclear fission to form strontium-93 ($^{93}_{38}\text{Sr}$) and xenon-139 ($^{139}_{54}\text{Xe}$) according to

$${}^{1}_{0}\text{n} + Z \rightarrow {}^{93}_{38}\text{Sr} + {}^{139}_{54}\text{Xe} + 2{}^{1}_{0}\text{n}.$$

Table 9.1 shows the binding energies of the strontium-93 and xenon-139 nuclei.

Table 9.1

nucleus | binding energy / $\text{J}$
$^{93}_{38}\text{Sr}$ | $1.25 \times 10^{-10}$
$^{139}_{54}\text{Xe}$ | $1.81 \times 10^{-10}$

The fission of $1.00\text{ mol}$ of $Z$ releases $1.77 \times 10^{13}\text{ J}$ of energy.

Determine the binding energy per nucleon, in $\text{MeV}$, of $Z$.
